To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the reaction rate constant of SiC formation was obtained by the kinetic study of SiC formation on graphite using N2-CO and N2-H2-SiCO gas mixtures.

the formation rate of the SiC layer increases with decreasing partial pressure of the CO gas and increasing temperature, and SiC whiskers form by a catalytic reaction in the liquid Fe-based nanospheres.

SiC was successfully formed on the graphite surface through the chemical vapor deposition method using SiO gas, which is a by-product in the reduction of SiO2 with CO gas, and the formation rate of the SiC increased with the increasing temperatures and with the decreasing concentrations of CO gas.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the formation of SiO gas and SiC on a carbon surface through the reaction of SiO with C.
the reaction kinetics of the formation of Si–C composite materials on graphite using N2-CO or N2CO-H2 gas mixtures.
the reaction between SiC and CO gas.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the SiC formation reaction is strongly affected by the partial pressure of SiO and CO gases, and by the temperature.
the reaction between SiC and SiO gas is a first-order reaction with respect to SiO.

the reaction rate constants of the SiC formation reaction on the graphite surface were successfully determined by the present study, and the SiC whisker formation mechanism on a graphite surface was proposed.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the SiC formation on a graphite surface is promoted by the catalytic effect of Fe-based nanodrops, and that the SiC whiskers are grown by the SiO gas supply from the Fe-based nanodrop to the graphite surface.
the formation of the SiC whiskers can be promoted through the reaction with the CO gas and the catalytic reaction with liquid Fe.
the SiC formation rate on a graphite surface was controlled by the chemical reaction between SiO and C.
The main takeaway from our work is that
SiO and CO gases are the main reactants in the SiC formation on the graphite surface, and the reaction rate is affected by the partial pressure of CO.
the SiC formation rate on a graphite surface is strongly affected by the partial pressure of CO and the presence of H2 gas in the SiO gas.
the SiC formation rate on the graphite surface was increased under a N2-CO- H2-SiO atmosphere.
